We have applied first template 324324, got precursors: product1: "Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1" and "Nc1ccccc1N". That seems plausible: the amide N attached to phenyl? Actually original target had ...C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N (an anilide with an aniline). The first step likely disconnection of the amide to give aniline (Nc1ccccc1N) and a carboxylic acid derivative (the rest). Good.

Second template 1914396 applied to the acid derivative gave two fragments: "Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2)cc1" and "O=C(O)CC(=O)O". So we broke the double bond? Actually we got a benzaldehyde fragment and a succinic acid? The second fragment is O=C(O)CC(=O)O (malonic acid). So we have now three molecules: the first fragment still contains sulfonamide and a benzaldehyde (C=O) attached to phenyl. The third template 733 to apply to that fragment maybe to disconnect sulfonamide? Let's check if template 733 matches the fragment "Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2)cc1". Use check.
